x: Seven went down for the count, and Jumbo Masters set off in a respectable sixth place. Jumbo had his usual steady run and gained a further position, it was then that Mac had his go!.

Ted Smith, Hugh McGreechan and Charlie Walker are the proud fathers of newly born sons, whilst John Keown and Eric Gebbett and Jumbo Masters are equally proud of their daughters---perhaps we'll have a ladies section yet !

Jumbo Masters, with a time better than two of our 'A' team had gained the 'B' team two places. Don Maclean ran well, despite the agonised look on his face and the jack-tar sway of his body near the finish, but Terry Stacey had taken the Valley back into fourth place.

Heiburg (Woodford) Jumbo Masters, on the next stage, pegged back the previous leaders and so retained 3rd place. Aylesford, after an excellent run by Frank Sando had moved up from 17th to 4th, just behind.

Ken Miller, Jumbo Masters and Symons of Hercules as a result lost 200 yds or so through going off course. Towl (HHH) was a comfortable winner in 29:53, with Shippen (31:30), Miller (31:35) and Masters (31:40), 3rd, 4th, 5th, Charlie Dabbs (34:40) could not overcome the going and finished an uncharacteristic 15th.
Our boys got away to a good start and Black, Miller, Brown, Dabbs and Johnston were soon prominent, with Masters and Dooley further back but well positioned.
